catch: The summary table in the Q3 pricing one-pager dropped the [ESTIMATE] marker from the 'pays back in 90 days' row; the long-form draft carried it but the table did not, laundering an estimate into a flat claim.
pattern: evidence markers get lost when a writer summarizes marked prose into a table or bullet list
rule: diff the marker counts between the source draft and every rendered output, not just confirm the markers exist in the source

catch: The Northwind Analytics landing page footer carried an internal scoring phrase ('validator score 9 of 9') in customer-facing copy, inherited verbatim from the source brief.
pattern: renders faithfully inherit internal vocabulary from the source brief and carry it into customer-facing output
rule: run the deny-list scrub on the source brief, not only on the final render; one internal-vocabulary hit is a defect no quality score overrides

catch: The stated calendar strategy was 2 carousels / 2 text / 1 poll per week, but week 1 shipped 1 carousel / 3 text / 1 poll; the highest-engagement format was under-allocated in the opening week even though the monthly aggregate matched.
pattern: a builder states a format/frequency distribution then writes individual units that do not match it per period
rule: verify per-unit allocation against the stated distribution for each period; aggregate intent does not guarantee per-period compliance

catch: The brief stated 'founded in 2012' and elsewhere '15 years in business'; 2026 minus 2012 is 14, not 15, and the founding year was inferred rather than sourced.
pattern: a derived numeric claim is carried into a deliverable without re-deriving it, and the arithmetic no longer holds
rule: recompute every derived number at the point it is restated; a year/age/count that is inferred must be sourced or recomputed, never copied as-is

catch: Cited a file hash from the builder's submission message instead of the hash printed by the tool in the same step; the on-disk file had been edited after the builder's message, so the cited hash was stale.
pattern: composing a verdict from a peer's stated value instead of from one's own tool output in the same step
rule: quote the hash from the tool output in the current step; if the tool has not run at compose time, defer the verdict until it has

catch: A thought-leadership post opened with a specific-dollar anecdote ('we saved a client 47,000 dollars in March') presented as a real event with no named entity and no [ESTIMATE] marker; the hook was invented to illustrate a point.
pattern: thought-leadership hooks use invented scenarios that read as real because of specific numbers and dated framing
rule: flag specific-number anecdotes that lack a named real entity as potential fabrication; require a 'composite example' frame or an evidence marker
